title: Screen Time for Little Kids: Less, Together, On Purpose
hook: For babies under about 18 months the AAP says skip screens except video chat. For toddlers and preschoolers, keep it limited and high-quality, watch together, and protect sleep, meals, and play.
key_points: Under about 18 months: avoid screen media other than video chatting with family.
18-24 months: if you introduce media, choose high-quality content and watch it together.
Ages 2-5: keep screen time limited (around an hour a day of high-quality content) and co-view.
Protect what matters: sleep, meals, physical activity, and hands-on play come first — make a Family Media Plan.
content_html: Screens aren't all-or-nothing, but for the youngest kids the AAP keeps it simple: babies under about 18 months should skip screen media other than video chatting with loved ones, which is interactive and social. Between 18 and 24 months, if you do introduce media, choose high-quality content and watch it together rather than handing the device over. For ages 2 to 5, keep it limited — around an hour a day of high-quality programming — and co-view so you can talk about what you're seeing.
extra_html: The bigger idea is to protect what builds young brains: sleep, mealtimes, physical activity, and unstructured, hands-on play. The AAP suggests making a Family Media Plan so screen rules fit your family and stay consistent. This is general educational information from the AAP — your pediatrician can help you tailor media habits to your child.

related.title: Play Is How Young Children Learn
related.hook: For young children, play isn't a break from learning — it is the learning, building language, problem-solving, and social skills all at once.

related.title: Reading Together: Start at Birth
related.hook: You don't need to wait until your child can follow a story. Reading aloud from birth builds language, attention, and your bond — and even a few interactive minutes a day counts.

flashcards.explanation_html: Under about 18 months, AAP advises avoiding screen media other than video chatting with loved ones.

flashcards.prompt: For toddlers and preschoolers, what two habits make screen time healthier?
flashcards.back_html: Choose high-quality content and watch it together (co-view). Keep the amount limited, and protect sleep, meals, physical activity, and play.
